# <span id="aanchor95"></span> Gas Quality Source Editor

[&lt;&lt; Back](Gas%20Quality%20Source%20Editor.md#Tabs) \| <a href="#" class="selected">Main</a> \| [Source Analysis](Source%20Analysis%20Tab.md) \| [Characteristic](Characteristic%20Tab.md) \| [Service](Service%20Tab.md)

## Main Tab

The Main tab in the Gas Quality Source Editor shows basic information about the source, such as the measurement area, import ID, and analysis type. The fields that are shaded in gray such as System Name, Analysis Type, and Source Meter Number are read-only.

By default, the only fields required to save a new source are Source Number and Reason.

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Data Field Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Details">

The following items are available on the Main tab of the Gas Quality Source Editor:

- **System Name** - Displays the name of the system the source belongs to

- **Import ID** - If applicable, enter the Import ID. This is used if importing data from a third party and the source number in the file is different than the source number that is setup in FLOWCAL. This will tell FLOWCAL what source to import the data to. It can be used with text file imports or Transaction Queue.

- **Analysis Type** - Read-only field that is set to gas when the source is created

- **TESTit Enable** - This field by default is set to No when a source is created. You can update this field to Yes for this source to be utilized with TESTit Integrated. If you do not have TESTit Integrated, this field is hidden.

  This feature is supported by TESTit v2 Integrated only. Once this field is set to Yes, it cannot be changed due to the audit trail and the ability to link TESTit tasks to this source. Test reports are available through the Tools \> Test Reports menu on the Gas Quality Source Editor.

- **FWS** - See: [Full Wellstream Factor](Full%20Wellstream%20Factor.md)

- <span id="DefaultAnalysis"></span>**Default Analysis** - On startup of a new well the user may assign the meter to a default gas quality source until the first samples are collected and verified. Assigning a meter to a default source (a source with this flag set) generates exception 56 on the meter at the start of the assignment indicating that the meter is using a default analysis. Later, the meter is reassigned to a real source and the exception is cleared.

  If the user chooses to enter non-default analysis into the source and change the Default Analysis flag to No, the user will need to manually ignore the exception.

- **Enable HCDP** - If checked, FLOWCAL will calculate the hydrocarbon dew point. Sample pressure, sample temperature, absolute or gauge, and atmospheric pressure must be provided for the calculation as well as the sample composition.

  HCDP is the temperature at a given pressure at which hydrocarbons will start to condense out. The calculation methods used are Sandler-Clark or Lomic. Lomic requires a separate license.

  The HCDP service (FcSrvHCDPQueueProcessor.exe) must be installed and running for these calculations to be done.

- **Enable CCT** - If checked, FLOWCAL will calculate the cricondentherm. Mole percents are required for this calculation. Cricondentherm is the highest temperature at any pressure at which hydrocarbons will condense out.

  The HCDP service (FcSrvHCDPQueueProcessor.exe) must be installed and running for these calculations to be done.

- **Enable Rollups** - All quality samples are stored at the data resolution they are generated (4-minute, hourly, daily, monthly, quarterly, etc.). When Enable Rollups is checked, and the Type is Chromatograph or RTU Average, the quality samples are averaged and rolled up into daily and monthly averages. This could be useful for users handling daily and weekly chromatographs that need to report averages for a period. If the Type is Gas Analysis, the quality is copied directly to the rollup tables.

  The rollups service (FcSrvGQAnlRollup.exe) must be installed and running. To view the result of the source rollups, go to Open \> Rollup Viewers \> Source Analysis Rollups.

- **Save Hourly Rollups** - If checked, the hourly rollup data will be saved to the database; otherwise, it is calculated on rollup, but discarded, saving database space.

- **Replace Original Only** - When checked, during imports of quality samples, only the revision zero or original data is replaced. Edits to the data are retained and are used when a sample is applied.

- **Remove Overlapping Edits** - When checked (default), during imports of quality samples, existing samples are replaced. Any edits that overlap the imported data are truncated to end where the new analysis begins and resume after it ends.

- **Snap Before/Snap After**\* - If the effective date of a record (especially a chromatograph hourly record) is provided and is not exactly at the top of the hour (ex: 08:00:05) but is within the range specified before and after the hour, it will "snap" to the top of the hour (ex: 08:00:05 would be snapped to 08:00:00). (See: [Snap Before/Snap After Details](../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Snap%20Before-Snap%20After.md))

- **Date Rule**\* - Used to specify rules for setting the effective date on analysis during the import process when an effective date is not provided, or the Override Effective Date on Import is enabled.

- **Override Effective Date on Import** - Used in conjunction with the Date Rule. If an effective date is provided on import, this option must be checked to override the date and apply the Date Rule specified. Otherwise, the effective date provided on import will be used.

- **Time Rule**\* - Used in conjunction with the Date Rule option, the Time Rule will define what hour to use for the override. When using the Date Rule, a time of midnight will be used by default unless a Time Rule is specified.

- **Measurement Area** - Select a measurement area from the drop-down or, with the correct privileges, click the New button to create a new Measurement Area. Measurement areas are managed from the Measurement Area Editor.

- **Data Stream** - Informational field used to denote a data collection system or source

- **Source Meter Number** - A read-only field that displays the meter number that the source is receiving analysis from. This would be used if sending Online GC data from a meter to a source.

- **Custom Fields** - User-definable fields that can be used to accommodate company-specific information, such as division or field technician. All the labels are user-defined and are managed from the Custom Fields screen within the Settings Manager. Fields 1–5 are numeric and 6–10 are alphanumeric.

..\* The Date Rule and Time Rule options are only supported for file imports, not Transaction Queue; however, the Snap Before and Snap After options are supported by both.
